study.title: Automatic detection on intracranial aneurysm from digital subtraction angiography with cascade convolutional neural networks

imaging.modality_detail: 2D-DSA, matched frontal and lateral sequences acquired simultaneously; 1024 x 1024 DICOM
imaging.territory_detail: Intracranial aneurysms in the posterior communicating artery (PCoA) region of the internal carotid artery
imaging.frames_per_sequence: 6-12 frames selected per patient by radiologists

data_released.detail: Available from the corresponding author on reasonable request

annotation.annotator_expertise: Experienced radiologists; labels double confirmed by 3D-DSA

task.task_description: Two-stage CNN cascade: region localization stage locates the PCoA region, then a dual-input (frontal + lateral view) FPN detector identifies intracranial aneurysms vs. vessel overlaps, with a regional average grayscale suppression (RAGS) false-positive filter; patient-level aneurysm diagnosis derived from frame detections.
task.clinical_application: Computer-aided detection of intracranial aneurysms on 2D-DSA to assist physicians

temporal_evidence.quote: the relationship and information of each frame in an entire DSA sequence were not utilized

comparators: Rahmany et al. classical DIP method (MSER, SURF, SIFT)

G1.quote: the data set is limited that it only contained 261 patients with aneurysms in PCoA region

G2.quote: Transfer learning method [32] can be applied if we can obtain data of other ICA regions in the future

G3.quote: the relationship and information of each frame in an entire DSA sequence were not utilized

G4.quote: dual-input model can relatively remedy the information loss of single 2D-DSA image

G9.quote: more special patients should be employed for model training to improve the robustness of RLS

other_limitations: Strict any-frame patient-level evaluation indicator inflates false positives
RAGS heuristic not completely reasonable; causes some false negatives
Two-stage architecture is complicated and limited to a specific region
DSA is invasive; patients may not be willing to undergo it
future_work: Transfer learning to other ICA regions
Apply RNN on CNN features to combine DSA sequence context
End-to-end detector beyond a specific region
Consider widely accessible modalities such as MRA and CTA
Extend to other regions such as ACoA with more labeled data
Include more special patients in training to improve robustness
